cancellation_summary: 7 or more days prior 100%; 3-7 days prior 50%; no refund within 3 days
description: This semiprivate tour from Boston takes you north to historic Salem, famous for the 1692 witch trials. You'll visit the Witch Trials Memorial and explore the city's Puritan past. Beyond the hysteria, you'll discover Salem's prosperity during the "Old China Trade," which made it one of the wealthiest towns in the young U.S., as highlighted at the Salem Maritime National Historic Site. The itinerary includes 1.5 hours of free time for lunch and shopping for unique souvenirs, from magnets to spell ingredients, before your private return trip.

what_is_included_items.value: Entry tickets to the Witch House
Entry tickets to Charter St Cemetery

itinerary:
1. Pick Ups
Your guide will loop in an optimized route around Boston to pick up all the groups.

2. 50 min - Transfer to Salem
Ride to Salem in comfort with wifi on board!

3. 15 min - East India Square
Get situated, use the restroom, and get your first glimpse of Salem!

4. 25 min - Salem Common
At the Salem Common, stop by the Roger Conant Statue. Across the street, view the Salem Witch Museum as the Salem Witch Trials are introduced.

5. 40 min - Witch Trials Memorial
Hear the true story of the Salem Witch Trials. Learn about who the victims were, why and how they ended up there, and more.

6. 20 min - Old Burying Point (aka Charter St Cemetery)
See the oldest cemetery in Salem, where some of its earliest settlers are buried.

7. 10 min - Peabody House
See this historic Colonial Revival, built in the 1800s by one of Salem's merchants.

8. 15 min - Houdini Way
Learn about Harry Houdini's famous escape from the town jail.

9. 20 min - Bewitched Statue
Learn how a fire at the studio helped put Salem on the map!

10. 90 min - Break
Break for lunch and souvenir shopping.

11. 30 min - The Witch House
Go inside the Witch House, built in 1642. Judge Corwin of the Witch Trials once lived in this very home. Learn all about the Corwin Curse!

12. 15 min - Ropes Mansion
See the historic, 1700s-era mansion used in the filming of Hocus Pocus. Learn about the famous ghosts who haunt the building.

13. 20 min - Hamilton Hall
Stop by "America's First Red Carpet," at this dance hall named for the founding father.

14. 20 min - Chestnut Street
Walk one of Salem's most prestigious and historic streets. Learn stories of the wealthy mansions lining the street, built from the prosperous "Old China" trade.

15. 20 min - The Merchant
See the most haunted building in Salem, standing on the original foundation from when the infamous George Corwin owned the property.

16. 20 min - Derby Wharf
Drive by Salem's harbor while looking at the historic Derby Wharf. Learn how Salem became the richest town in the country through trade.

17. 10 min - Proctor's Ledge
See where the hangings during the Witch Trials actually took place.

18. 1 hour - Return to Boston
Ride in comfort back to Boston! Your guide will follow the same route for drop offs (first in, first out).
highlights:
Begin your historic journey with pickup and transport from Boston, heading north to the remarkable city of Salem. This city holds a permanent place in history due to the shocking witch trials of 1692. You’ll walk the streets where panic once reigned, gaining valuable perspective on the strict Puritan culture that defined life in early New England. We’ll pay our respects to the tragic events of the past with a poignant stop at the somber Witch Trials Memorial.

The history of Salem extends far beyond its darkest period. You will next uncover its era of tremendous wealth, which was fueled by the "Old China Trade." Salem’s powerful sailing vessels traveled to distant ports in Asia, returning with highly sought-after goods like tea, silk, and porcelain. This booming commerce established Salem as a major economic center in the newly formed United States and even produced America’s first millionaire. You can explore this maritime legacy firsthand at the Salem Maritime National Historic Site, seeing how global trade shaped the city's identity.

The itinerary includes an hour and a half of independent time for you to choose a local restaurant for lunch and browse the numerous shops for souvenirs. Salem's stores offer a wide variety of items, from classic magnets and T-shirts to more unusual treasures like tarot cards, spell ingredients, and occult charms. After your free time, we will continue exploring Salem’s most significant landmarks and cultural institutions before your comfortable, shared ride brings you back to your starting point at the end of the day.
check_in_details: You'll receive a text (or WhatsApp for non-US/Canada numbers) the afternoon before containing a 10-minute pickup window and guide details. Please be outside; your guide will not be able to come inside the lobby of your hotel.
what_to_bring: Comfortable walking shoes, money for lunch and souvenirs (most shops accept major credit cards).
special_requirements: Children under 8 years old or under 57 inches tall must have a proper car seat, per MA law. Please bring one if necessary. We do not provide car seats, and can not provide refunds day-of for lack of proper seating.
restrictions: This tour has a significant amount of walking and is not suitable for anyone who needs frequent breaks.
disclaimers: Salem is extremely crowded during the fall season, especially as Halloween approaches. Expect slow movement, busy attractions, and long lines at popular shops.
